text: dsh-token-usage-dashboard 是面向 DSH Web 的 Token 用量统计面板。它在设置页增加 Stats 界面，并从会话事件与历史日志汇总 token、请求、轮次、时长和模型数据，提供总量与峰值统计、每日或每周热力图、连续活跃天数、使用洞察及模型用量排行。主机端通过 connection.fetch 提供统计和重扫接口，并将快照保存在 DSH 原生 JSON 存储中。适合想查看 DSH 会话用量趋势和模型消耗的人；不需要额外账号或 API Key。

dsh-token-usage-dashboard adds a DSH Web token dashboard. It aggregates historical and live session usage, then shows token totals, daily or weekly heatmaps, activity streaks, insights, and model rankings. Snapshots use DSH JSON storage. No account or API key is needed.

dsh-token-usage-dashboard 的功能「会话用量汇总」：读取历史会话并持续处理新会话事件，汇总 Token、请求、轮数、时长、活跃日和连续天数。
dsh-token-usage-dashboard 的功能「每日与每周热力图」：在设置页显示最多 53 周的 Token 活动网格，可切换每日或每周视图，并通过悬停查看日期用量。
dsh-token-usage-dashboard 的功能「模型用量排行」：根据会话请求中的 provider/model 归属聚合 Token 用量，并在面板中按消耗量展示模型排名。
dsh-token-usage-dashboard 首次启动会扫描历史会话，并把统计快照写入 DSH 原生 JSON 存储；设置了 DSH_HOME 时也会用它确定旧式快照文件路径。

English | [简体中文](README.zh.md)

A Codex-style token usage dashboard for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh) Web UI:
5 stat cards + a GitHub-style activity heatmap (daily / weekly) + insights + per-model usage ranking.
The UI follows the DSH language setting: Chinese interface → Chinese dashboard, anything else → English.

dsh-token-usage-dashboard README · ✨ Features：- **5 stat cards**: total tokens / peak tokens (single day) / longest chat / current streak / longest streak; auto-shrinking one-line values
- **Heatmap**: 53×7 rolling grid (today pinned to the bottom-right corner), hover for `Aug 15, 2026: 273k tokens · 34 requests`;
  **Daily / Weekly** view toggle (weekly = bottom-up 7-cell bars, hover for the week total)
- **Insights**: total turns, LLM requests, sessions, active days, cache hit rate, avg tokens & duration per turn
- **Favorite models**: provider/model token ranking (Top 5) with ratio bars
- **Data source**: session logs (`assistant/message` usage + `request/header` model attribution + `turn/start`/`turn/end` durations), live incremental updates, persisted snapshot + incremental sync for fast restarts

dsh-token-usage-dashboard README · 🏗️ Architecture：- **Bundle form** (recommended for end users): installed via `dsh plugin add`; the npm package contains `lib/index.js` (host half) and `lib/client.js` (client half). The host half registers `GET /api/token-stats` and `POST /api/token-stats/rescan` through `connection.fetch`, behind the Web UI's Host/Origin and browser-session checks; the client half registers a "Settings → Stats" section and fetches the API.
- **Dynamic-plugin form** (for maintainers/iteration): `host.js` and `client.js` are pasted into `cordis_define` for in-session deployment without restarting the profile.

dsh-token-usage-dashboard README · 🏗️ Architecture：1. Host subscribes to `session/event` / `session/created` and also performs an initial backfill over historical session logs.
2. It folds `assistant/message.usage`, `request/header` model attribution, and `turn/start`/`turn/end` durations into in-memory aggregates.
3. Aggregates are periodically flushed to the host JSON storage unit `token_stats` (normally `<DSH_HOME>/storages/token_stats.json`); on restart the snapshot is loaded first, then only new events are incrementally folded. Older Harness versions expose `sessionPersistence.readFrom` for suffix reads; versions without it use `sessionQuery.readSession` to read the full log while still folding only new events.
4. The client polls `GET /api/token-stats` (2s while scanning, 30s after ready) and renders the dashboard.

dsh-token-usage-dashboard README · 🏗️ Architecture：An explicit rescan rebuilds from the current logs and replaces all aggregates only after every read succeeds. Repeated or simultaneous rescans do not accumulate history again. Live events received during replay are merged in sequence order. Normal restarts retain statistics for deleted sessions; an explicit rescan removes that history when the logs are gone. A failed rescan preserves the last complete result and reports an error.

dsh-token-usage-dashboard README · 🏗️ Architecture：Both forms use the host's `storage` / `storage.backend.json` services for persistence; the JSON backend owns its configured root, atomic writes and directory creation. These services are required for normal Cordis activation (verified on DSH Desktop 0.2.1-rc.2). When the native unit is empty, a readable legacy `token-stats/snapshot.json` is migrated without modifying the old file. Directly embedded hosts without native storage may still provide `fs`; its legacy path uses `profileContext.home`, or an explicit `dshHome`. Bundle additionally falls back to `DSH_HOME` / the OS user's `.dsh`; Dynamic without any known home stays in memory. The dynamic plugin continues to use the authenticated Harness RPC channel.

dsh-token-usage-dashboard README · 🏗️ Architecture：Enable only one form per host. Bundle and Dynamic share the `token_stats` storage unit, which permits one active handle at a time.

The plugin does not restrict Harness release numbers. Both host forms check the session-query APIs during activation; Bundle also requires the authenticated Fetch registry. Optional incremental reads keep their full-log fallback. Tested versions and the pinned test fixture are recorded separately from activation requirements.

dsh-token-usage-dashboard README · Tests：Run `npm ci && npm test` for regression tests covering both host implementations. The optional real-Harness HTTP and native-storage integration tests require Node 24 and a Harness source checkout; see [TESTING.md](TESTING.md) for commands, the pinned contract revision, and coverage limits.

dsh-token-usage-dashboard README · 🚀 Install (bundle)：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:solstice621/dsh-token-usage-dashboard
dsh --profile web   # restart to apply
```

Then open **Settings → Stats** for the full dashboard. Local install:
`dsh plugin --profile web add file:/path/to/dsh-token-usage-dashboard`.

> On first open the plugin scans all historical sessions (seconds to a minute), then updates
> in real time via `session/event`; the dashboard auto-refreshes every 30s — no manual action needed.

handy for iterating without restarting the profile):

dsh-token-usage-dashboard README · 🧑‍💻 Dynamic-plugin deployment (maintainers)：> ⚠️ The bundle and the dynamic plugin register the same settings section id (`token-stats`);
> don't run both at once — stop one before enabling the other.

dsh-token-usage-dashboard README · ✅ Acceptance checklist：- [ ] Settings → Stats: 5 equal-width cards, one-line values, aligned labels
- [ ] 53-column heatmap, today at bottom-right, year-month-day hover tips; Daily/Weekly toggle works
- [ ] Month axis aligned to columns; no horizontal scrollbar
- [ ] Insights (7 rows) and Top-5 model ranking with bars correct

dsh-token-usage-dashboard README · 🩺 Troubleshooting：| Symptom | Cause / fix |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm not found on PATH` | `dsh plugin` needs pnpm: `corepack enable pnpm` (bundled with Node ≥16.10) |
| Two "Stats" sections in Settings | bundle + dynamic plugin (toksta-5) both active; stop one |
| Plain text, no styles at all | CSS not injected: dynamic `styles` is a Client Builtin (`styles.insert(css)`), not `ctx.get('styles')`; bundle injects via `<style>` |
| Client render crash `ctx is not defined` | `ctx` only exists in `apply(ctx)`; components use the module-level timer bridge (`intervalRef = (cb, ms) => ctx.interval(...)`) |
| `service "timer" is not declared` | client has no timer Service; drop `inject: ['timer']` |
| Horizontal scrollbar flashes under the heatmap | old month-label `nowrap` text inflated scrollable overflow; container & month row are `overflow:hidden` now |
| `console.warn` throws | Host builtins only expose `console.log/error`; use `console.error` |
